old: *Soler* is followed by an infinitive. The form changes according to the subject: *suelo*, *sueles*, *suele*, *solemos*, *suelen*.
new: *Soler* is followed by an infinitive and changes with the subject: *Suelo caminar después de cenar*, but *Mis padres suelen cenar temprano*. Usually the present tense already says it is a habit; *soler* makes that explicit.
why: tip was a list of stray verb forms (and missing soléis for es-es): one natural sentence showing the point
